questions.q: In 'The Ass and the Load of Salt', why did the Ass fall in the river on purpose the second time?
choices: He remembered that the salt melted and his load got lighter
He was very thirsty after the long walk from the seashore
He wanted a cool bath in the river on such a hot day
He slipped again on the same smooth stone in the stream
questions.evidence: remembering what had happened at the ford, purposely let himself fall into the water

questions.q: In 'The Ass and the Load of Salt', why was the load of sponges so much heavier after the Ass fell?
choices: The sponges soaked up the water
The Merchant had added more sponges
The sponges had turned into wet salt
The Ass was too tired to carry them
questions.evidence: a load ten times heavier than before

questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Gnat', how did the Lion get hurt?
choices: He tore himself with his own claws
The Gnat stung him deep in the tail
He tripped and fell into a spider's web
Another lion came and attacked him

questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Gnat', what happened to the Gnat after he beat the Lion?
choices: He flew into a spider's web
He became the new king of beasts
He flew home to rest and to boast
The Lion caught him in his paw
questions.evidence: he flew straight into a spider's web

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Leap at Rhodes'?
choices: Deeds count, not boasting words
It is good to travel to foreign lands
Always bring witnesses when you jump
Practice your jumping every day

questions.q: In 'The Cock and the Jewel', what did the Cock say he would rather have than the jewel?
choices: A single grain of barleycorn
A bigger and shinier jewel
A soft new nest for his hen
A cool drink of fresh water
questions.evidence: I would choose a single grain of barleycorn before all the jewels in the world

questions.q: In 'The Monkey and the Camel', why did the Camel start to dance?
choices: He envied the praise the Monkey got
King Lion asked him to dance next
The Monkey dared him to dance
He wanted to frighten the animals
questions.evidence: The praise that was showered on the Monkey made the Camel envious.

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Monkey and the Camel'?
choices: Do not try to ape your betters
Dancing is good for everyone
Camels are the best dancers
Always obey the Lion, your king
questions.evidence: Do not try to ape your betters.
